page: Microsoft Azure D16alds_v6 is an x86_64 server belonging to the Daldv6 family, powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The memory configuration consists of 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 945 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is premium storage capable.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core metrics, falls within the average range. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance for cached small-block reads and large-block writes, but large-block uncached reads are relatively weak, placing in the bottom 25%. Text processing and small-model LLM text generation are notable strengths, scoring in the top tier.

The D16alds_v6 offers a specialized hardware profile that trades memory capacity for compute density. With only 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, it provides a cost-efficient alternative for workloads that require high CPU clock speeds and fast local NVMe storage without the overhead of a large memory footprint. However, the low memory-to-vCPU ratio and weak uncached large-block memory read bandwidth represent clear tradeoffs for memory-intensive applications.

This server is suited for compute-bound tasks with moderate memory requirements, such as software compilation, text processing, web serving, and small-scale language model inference. The integrated 945 GB NVMe SSD also makes it appropriate for database operations and localized file processing where high-speed storage is required.
